Majestic class aircraft carriers – naval encyclopedia Skip to content United Kingdom: 5 light fleet aircraft carriers: HMS Majestic, Terrible, Powerful, Magnificient, Hercules, Powerful, 1 more cancelled (1944-1999) British Cold War Carriers: Majestic class | Centaur class | HMS Victorious | HMS Eagle | HMS Ark Royal | HMS Hermes | CVA-01 project | Invincible class | HMS Argus | Queen Elisabeth class (planned) The majestic class were part of the 1942 Design Light Fleet Carrier programme, the most ambitious of the Royal Navy in WW2.
The six remaining Light Fleet hulls were originally planned as standard Colossus-class ships, but carrier-based aviation grew up in size since 1942.
All three ships were laid up after the war, but were rebuilt into the Courageous-class aircraft carriers during the 1920s.

HMS Activity (D94) British Escort Carrier - Destination's Journey Skip to content Search Search This Site HMS Activity (D94) British Escort Carrier HMS Activity D94 Laid down as the refrigerated cargo ship Telemachus for the Alfred Holt Line, but taken over by the Admiralty in February 1941, for conversion to an escort carrier, HMS Activity was commissioned on 29 September 1942. Until August 1944, she escorted convoys, where her aircraft participated in the sinking of two U-boats and damaged three others.
